sources.title: Becharof National Wildlife Refuge: About Us
sources.method: Read actual cached HTML text: Becharof Lake, Wilderness and Kanatak Trail sections.
observations: Page uses Becharof Lake and explicitly places Severson Peninsula between Island Arm and the open water. Ruth Lake and Ruth River appear separately.
No formal GNIS/BGN record or naming-adjudication date established.

sources.title: Guide Use Areas within Alaska Peninsula and Becharof NWRs
sources.agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Region 7, Division of Realty and Natural Resources
sources.method: Independently rendered original single-page PDF at 1400px overview and 1350px full-lake/neighbor crop; compared my full 104-position source outline.
observations: Broad west-to-east main basin plus southeast Island Arm correspond to the whole source outline. The eastern peninsula/neck structure agrees qualitatively.

Upper and Lower Ugashik lakes remain distinct southwest basins; Puale and Portage bays lie beyond intervening land east/southeast. Islands visible inside Becharof are filled by the no-hole source polygon.
Qualitative whole-water identity supported; exact shoreline, small land/water margins and numeric overlap were not established.

sources.title: Egegik River & Becharof Lake System: RDI application
sources.agency: State of Alaska Department of Natural Resources; official original hosted by U.S. Bureau of Land Management
sources.method: Read cached PDF text on pages 1, 2, 8 and 11; independently rendered/viewed page 26 at 1300px.
observations: Application dated 2017-12-28 distinguishes Becharof Lake, Egegik River, Ruth Lake and the unnamed outlet of Ruth Lake; page 8 treats Island Arm as Becharof Lake.
Naknek map excerpt is dated 1952, scale 1:250,000, with Becharof northern shore and label between 157 W and 156 W along 58 N. It is partial coverage, not whole-perimeter proof.
Compilation is secondary corroboration only; no present legal ownership or naming determination inferred and raw compilation excluded.

sources.title: Mobile Core Bathurst Caribou Management Zone
sources.agency: Government of the Northwest Territories, Environment and Natural Resources
sources.method: Inspected original page 2 map labels and embedded registration; independently rebuilt ellipsoidal Lambert transform from GPTS/LPTS/BBox/WKT, transformed all 173 coordinates, viewed complete 1350px overlay and 1300px southwest crop.
observations: Repeated MacKay labels align with the west basin, connecting main reach and long northeast arm. Nodinka Narrows, Warburton Bay and Portage Bay provide shape checks; Courageous, Matthews, Dumbell, Snake and King lakes remain adjacent separate mapped waters.
The southwest red boundary crosses the two-line Lockhart River label. Its Lockhart text center is inside; its River text center is just outside. Three nearby Lockhart Lake label centers are outside.

The southwest reach follows connected mapped water near these labels. Label placement alone does not establish a river/lake name boundary or prove a two-lake composite. Full-polygon scalar MacKay name remains on hold.
Big Island and other islands are absent from the no-hole input. Tiny control-fit residuals verify map registration consistency only.

sources.title: Tursujuq
sources.method: Read original cached HTML park overview and The Goulet section.
observations: Current retrieved page uses Lac Tasiujaq and Lake Tasiujaq, describes brackish tidal water, and says The Goulet connects it to Hudson Bay.
This is direct park-use evidence, not a legal registry extract. The water cannot be assumed fresh or isolated from its baseline Lake category.

sources.title: Règlementation sur la pêche dans les parcs nationaux du Nunavik: Parc national Tursujuq 2024–2025
sources.agency: Nunavik Parks; Annex 1 map produced by Québec Ministère des Forêts, de la Faune et des Parcs, Direction des parcs nationaux
sources.publication_date: 2024–2025 guide; Annex 1 map copyright fourth quarter 2015
sources.method: Independently rendered/viewed page 6 overview at 1400px and entire target-water crop at 1370px; compared my complete 105-position source outline.
observations: Annex 1 labels Lac Guillaume-Delisle south of Umiujaq. Narrow northern reach, east-side embayments, broad triangular southern basin and southwest Le Goulet spur match the source outline qualitatively.
Hudson Bay is west; the separate inland two-basin Lac à l’Eau Claire is not part of this feature. Islands are present on the map but missing from the input geometry.

The map footer is fourth-quarter 2015 and scale 1:850,000; the guide is 2024–2025. Treating its map name as a 2024 naming decision would be incorrect. Exact Le Goulet cutoff and shoreline are unverified.

sources.title: Recovery Strategy for the Harbour Seal, Lacs des Loups Marins subspecies (Phoca vitulina mellonae)
sources.agency: Fisheries and Oceans Canada; Species at Risk Act Recovery Strategy Series
observations: The text explicitly pairs Tasiujaq and Wiyâshâkimî with former Guillaume-Deslisle and à l’Eau Claire in that order, independently bridging the older map label to current park usage.
The page spells Deslisle; the map spells Delisle. Preserve the discrepancy rather than assert exact spelling equality. It provides no formal naming-decision date or registry identifier.

sources.title: Guide Use Areas within Alaska Peninsula and Becharof NWRs
sources.method: Read actual cached media HTML title, date/author, exact downloadable file links and license field; hashed staged PDF against original.
observations: The media page title matches the map, credits Scott McGee, gives March 7 2012, and explicitly lists Public Domain.
Its file links point to exactly https://www.fws.gov/sites/default/files/documents/2024-04/3.pdf; a PDF link declares length=2153038. Staged file bytes match the acquired original SHA-256.
License receipt applies to this guide-use-area map only. Other raw maps, the State application and cached HTML are not approved for redistribution by this observation.

sources.title: Terms of Use
sources.method: Read actual cached HTML terms paragraph.
observations: Public-domain statement covers all Natural Earth raster/vector versions and permits modification and electronic dissemination. The baseline and source properties attribute the selected geometry to Natural Earth 5.0.0 1:10m.
This establishes selected-geometry redistribution scope; it does not license the independent Canadian maps or the State application.

publication_scope: Own factual extraction and hashes only. Raw source maps/crops stay outside this review. Separately staged FWS PDF has an exact-file Public Domain receipt.
